title: Wealth inequality measurement and social mobility support
asked: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh asked whether wealth in owner-occupied public housing is treated differently from private housing in wealth inequality measures, and how that affects economic resilience and the wealth Gini. Ms Mariam Jaafar asked what measures sustain or improve upward mobility for current and future cohorts.
asked_by: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh and Ms Mariam Jaafar
response: Mr Jeffrey Siow said real wages have risen across all income levels, income inequality has decreased, and social mobility remains strong. He said wealth inequality is hard to measure, so Singapore combines Household Expenditure Survey data with administrative records, estimates property at fair market value, and does not differentiate public/private or owner-occupied/non-owner-occupied housing in the wealth Gini because it is a stock measure. He said the top 1% hold about 14% of household wealth and the top 5% about 33%, that this is the first wealth Gini compilation with the next survey planned for 2028, and that there are no plans for extra powers to require more granular asset disclosures. On mobility, he cited early intervention, preschool, schools, SkillsFuture, the Progressive Wage Model, Workfare and ComLink+, and on property tax he cited progressive rates and deferral mechanisms for asset-rich, income-poor seniors.

key_points.point: Real wages rose across all income levels over the past decade, with the highest growth for lower-income workers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: over the past decade, real wages have risen across all income levels, with wage growth highest for lower-income workers.

key_points.point: Social mobility between generations remains strong.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: Social mobility between generations remains strong.

key_points.point: Wealth inequality is difficult to measure accurately in most countries.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: Most countries face challenges in measuring wealth inequality accurately.

key_points.point: Singapore combines Household Expenditure Survey data with administrative records.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: We have made our best effort by combining survey data from the Household Expenditure Survey with administrative records.

key_points.point: The top 1% hold about 14% of total household wealth, and the top 5% hold about 33%.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: The top 1% hold about 14% of total household wealth, while the top 5% holds about 33%.

key_points.point: This is the first compilation of the wealth Gini coefficient, with no historical series.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: This is our first compilation of the wealth Gini coefficient and we do not have a historical series.

key_points.point: The next Household Expenditure Survey is planned for 2028.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: The next cycle of the Household Expenditure Survey is planned for 2028.

key_points.point: There are no plans to seek additional legislative or administrative powers for more granular asset disclosures solely for inequality measurement.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: We have no plans at this point to seek additional legislative or administrative powers to require more granular asset disclosures solely for inequality measurement.

key_points.point: Wealth is taxed through less mobile assets like property and motor vehicles, to reduce susceptibility to cross-border movement and tax planning.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: Our approach is to tax wealth in ways that are less susceptible to cross-border movement and tax planning, while preserving competitiveness.

key_points.point: Asset-rich but income-poor seniors have deferral mechanisms for property tax payments.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: For asset-rich but income-poor seniors, we provide deferral mechanisms for property tax payments to ease cash-flow pressures.

key_points.point: The mobility strategy is to intervene early, provide support through life and ensure wage progression.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: Our strategy is to intervene early, provide support through life and ensure wage progression.

key_points.point: The Ministry has not done simulations separating investment property from owner-occupied property.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: On whether or not we have done simulations on separating investment of property from owner-occupied property, we have not done so.

key_points.point: The Government remains open to shifting from work to wealth taxation.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: On tax burden, whether or not we will shift from work to wealth taxation, I think, we remain open.

left_open: How liquidity differences from resale conditions and use-of-proceeds rules are taken into account in assessing households' economic resilience.
Whether the Government has targets for upward mobility rates.
How children from lower-income households are specifically protected from AI and technological shifts.
Whether additional safeguards beyond existing deferral mechanisms are planned for retirees.
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered wealth data measurement, social mobility, property tax pressures on asset-rich retirees, and shifting taxation from work to wealth.
